open_points.subject: A13 monotonic instants
open_points.text: its instants — when it began, its last request, when its confirmation was shown — and its expiry at the latest are held as readings of that monotonic clock
open_points.question: What is the representation, unit and comparison precision of a monotonic reading, including at the exact 8-hour, 30-minute and 10-minute boundaries?
options: Integer nanoseconds from an unspecified monotonic epoch
Integer microseconds or milliseconds from an unspecified monotonic epoch
A duration-capable opaque monotonic-instant type
Floating-point seconds
open_points.default_guess: Use opaque monotonic instants backed by integer nanoseconds and compare without rounding.

witness.initial: A confirmation is shown just under ten minutes before a submission.
events: Registry represents elapsed monotonic time at a precision that cannot represent the remaining fraction exactly.
The owner submits at the first representable reading around the ten-minute boundary.
outcomes: The reading rounds below ten minutes and the submission may proceed.
The reading rounds to ten minutes and the submission is refused as expired.
witness.observer: The owner submitting the confirmed action

open_points.subject: A13 clock readings per owner operation
open_points.text: Validity is checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1)
open_points.question: Does one owner request take one shared monotonic reading for session validity, idle refresh and confirmation age, or may those decisions take separate readings? The same question must be answered for showing a confirmation and for each cleanup pass.
options: One monotonic snapshot per request and one per cleanup pass
Separate readings for session validity, confirmation validity and last-request update
One request reading, but a separate reading when a confirmation is shown
open_points.default_guess: Take one shared monotonic reading at admission for every time comparison and session-time update caused by that request; take one snapshot for each cleanup pass.

witness.initial: A valid session carries a confirmation whose ten-minute limit is about to be reached.
events: The request's session check reads the clock just before the confirmation limit.
The confirmation check would read the clock just after the limit if it takes a second reading.
outcomes: With one shared reading, the confirmation is still valid and the action can be accepted.
With separate readings, the session passes but the confirmation is refused as expired.

open_points.subject: A13 suspend-inclusive monotonic backend
open_points.text: the process's monotonic clock, which a change of the wall clock does not move and which counts the time the host or its VM was suspended
open_points.question: Which generated clock backend provides a monotonic reading that includes host or VM suspension on every supported deployment platform?
options: Use an operating-system suspend-inclusive monotonic clock such as a boot-time clock
Wrap platform-specific suspend-inclusive clocks behind the emitted clock port
Use an ordinary monotonic clock even on platforms where suspension is excluded
open_points.default_guess: Use a platform-specific suspend-inclusive monotonic source behind the emitted clock port and reject unsupported deployments.
consequences: Preserves the requirement portably at the cost of backend variants
Can let sessions outlive a suspension and therefore violates the accepted guarantee
open_points.requirement: which a change of the wall clock does not move and which counts the time the host or its VM was suspended, so a session does not outlive a suspension

open_points.subject: A13 sign-in refusal limit
open_points.text: the five refusals of rule 3 are `SIGN_IN_REFUSAL_LIMIT`.
open_points.rule: Таблица выше — исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`, настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: The passage must name this value through the constant path, for example as `the imported SIGN_IN_REFUSAL_LIMIT constant`, rather than naming the bare symbol.

open_points.subject: A13/A16 confirmation after a same-byte re-upload
open_points.text: the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.
open_points.question: What state distinguishes the upload named by a confirmation from a later upload containing the same bytes: does an accepted upload clear the pending confirmation, or must the confirmation also bind an upload-generation identity?
options: Every accepted upload clears the pending import confirmation
Bind the confirmation to a per-upload generation identity as well as the file digest
Treat a same-byte re-upload as the same confirmed file
open_points.default_guess: Clear the pending import confirmation whenever an upload is accepted.

witness.initial: A session holds an uploaded file and a pending import confirmation bound to its digest and picks.
events: The owner uploads the same bytes again in that session.
The old uploaded file is replaced, but the new file has the same digest.
The owner submits the earlier confirmation value.
outcomes: The digest and every expressly listed bound input still match, so the new same-byte file is accepted.
Required test 3 requires the confirmation to be refused even when the new file has the same bytes.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation-input digest
open_points.text: its inputs — for the import, the file's digest and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never as the values themselves
open_points.question: What exact typed serialization and field order is used before hashing the confirmation inputs, including names, aliases and Customer values that A16 says the confirmation applies?
options: Canonical typed tuples with length-prefixed fields in an explicitly listed order
Canonical JSON with fixed field names, ordering and Unicode handling
Concatenated textual values with separators
open_points.default_guess: Use a canonical typed, length-prefixed serialization whose field order is declared by the exact contract.
consequences: Unambiguous across empty values, variable-length values and types
Interoperable if canonicalization and Unicode rules are fully fixed
Simple but permits ambiguous encodings unless escaping and typing are separately fixed
open_points.requirement: the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing else

open_points.subject: A16 import timestamp
open_points.text: An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers, the Customers it makes, the migration closure (M10) and its one audit entry (M09) in one transaction.
open_points.question: How many UTC wall-clock readings does an accepted import take, and must every new Customer, the migration closure and the audit entry receive one identical import instant?
options: Take one wall-clock reading for the whole import and reuse it for every newly recorded instant
Take one reading per newly created record
Take separate readings for domain records, the closure and the audit entry
open_points.default_guess: Take one UTC wall-clock reading after final validation and reuse it throughout the transaction.

witness.initial: An import creates two Customers, a migration closure and an audit entry.
events: The transaction remains open across a wall-clock tick.
Registry assigns the records their written instants.
outcomes: All records carry one identical import instant from one reading.
Customers, closure and audit entry carry different instants from separate readings.
witness.observer: The owner reading the imported Customers and audit log

open_points.subject: A16 file digest guarantee
open_points.text: The mapping names the file by its digest.
open_points.question: Must this digest be collision-resistant and computed over the exact received file bytes, or may it be a checksum or a digest of parsed or normalized content?
options: A collision-resistant digest of the exact received file-part bytes
A collision-resistant digest of canonical parsed content
A non-cryptographic checksum of the bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require a collision-resistant digest of the exact received file-part bytes; generation may then select the concrete approved algorithm.

witness.initial: A mapping and confirmation exist for one uploaded byte sequence.
events: A different byte sequence is uploaded that produces the same weak or normalization-based digest.
outcomes: The different file is treated as the mapped file because its digest matches.
A collision-resistant exact-byte identity causes the different file to be refused.
witness.observer: The owner and the resulting production store

open_points.subject: A19 rendering of non-text stored values
open_points.text: a value that is not text in the text it is shown as
open_points.question: Which textual representations do owner-interface contracts use for non-text stored values such as UTC instants, dates, ordinals, booleans, absent values and enum members?
options: Canonical machine-oriented forms such as ISO 8601 and enum values
Localized owner-facing forms
A distinct representation chosen independently by each page
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical, locale-independent textual forms fixed by the owner-interface contracts.
consequences: Stable across pages, tests and locales
More readable to the owner but requires locale and time-zone decisions
Allows inconsistent displays and makes the required escaping tests underspecified
open_points.requirement: The owner interface renders every stored value as text: escaped for the place it appears in, never as markup or script, whoever wrote it.

open_points.subject: A19 single-renderer coverage
open_points.text: Every page is made by one renderer, so this shows it for every stored value, whoever wrote it and whichever way it came in, the import file's included.
open_points.question: How is the claim that every owner page uses the one renderer established beyond exercising `_render_owner_page` with representative values?
options: A factory check rejects owner-page construction outside the renderer
Generated routing and page contracts expose only the renderer as a page-construction path
Runtime tests enumerate every owner route and verify renderer use
open_points.default_guess: Use a factory check for construction-path exclusivity plus route-level tests for representative contexts.
consequences: Directly proves the architectural invariant, including future pages
Makes the renderer boundary structural in generated contracts
Can miss a newly added or conditionally reached route
open_points.requirement: Every page is made by one renderer

open_points.subject: A21 security-review completeness evidence
open_points.text: Each APPLICABLE category's decisions have their own required tests, and those tests pass.
open_points.question: What required evidence shows that the references for each APPLICABLE category actually answer all of that category's stated questions, rather than merely existing and having unrelated tests that pass?
options: Require an explicit mapping from every category question to the decision and required test that answers it
Require a human review attestation for semantic coverage in addition to the lint checks
Treat existence of one accepted reference with passing tests as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit question-to-decision-to-test evidence mapping for every APPLICABLE category.
